name: Joint PAHO/TDR Impact Grants for Regional Priorities 2026-27 (elimination of communicable diseases in Latin America and the Caribbean)
amount: Up to US$30,000 per project
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica
eligibility: Open to researchers and institutions in Latin America and the Caribbean. Multicentre projects that actively engage public health authorities and promote regional collaboration get special consideration. Selected projects need approval from local ethics committees and the PAHO Ethics Review Committee (PAHOERC).
deadline: 2026-27 call closed 19 Aug 2026 (11:00 US ET).
status_note: Closed - awards pending; expect a further PAHO/TDR round in a later cycle (previous rounds 2022-23 and 2026-27).
what: Operational/implementation research on TB, opportunistic infections of advanced HIV disease (histoplasmosis, cryptococcal meningitis, leishmaniasis, Chagas, schistosomiasis), and AI applications for TB/HIV care delivery, follow-up, surveillance and decision-making.
mechanisms: Impact Grants for Regional Priorities (5 awards in 2026-27)
how: Via eTDR (who.my.site.com/etdr). First step for next round: build a multi-site team with a national TB/HIV programme partner and draft an AI/TB or advanced-HIV concept.

name: Joint WHO AFRO/TDR Impact Grants for Implementation Research for Regional Priorities 2026-27
funder: TDR (UNICEF/UNDP/World Bank/WHO Special Programme) with WHO Regional Office for Africa
amount: Up to US$15,000 per grant (co-funding encouraged)
duration: Max 12 months; must finish by end-2027, no no-cost extension
countries: Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: PI and most of the team must be based in an African Region institution (MoH/national disease programmes, universities, research institutes, NGOs). Must show prior operational/implementation research experience or training (e.g., TDR IR Toolkit or IR MOOC). Needs an acknowledgement letter from the relevant programme manager and, for health-centre studies, an authorization letter. Early-career, women and LDC applicants encouraged. English, French or Portuguese. One-page CV.
deadline: 2026-27 call closed 15 Sep 2026 (17:00 CEST); results within ~3 months. Next AFRO call expected in the 2027-28 cycle (typically announced mid-year).
status_note: Closed - deadline passed 15 Sep 2026; the scheme continues despite WHO budget cuts, so prepare for the next round.
what: Small implementation-research grants on infectious diseases of poverty in the African Region: person-centred PHC delivery (TB, malaria, NTDs), health-system bottlenecks incl. digital health and appropriate AI-supported tools, and climate/One Health/AMR/WASH.
mechanisms: Impact Grants for Regional Priorities (competitive call via eTDR portal)
how: Create an account on the eTDR Community Site (who.my.site.com/etdr), complete the IR MOOC now to meet the experience requirement, secure a programme-manager acknowledgement letter, and watch afro.who.int / tdr.who.int/grants for the next call.

name: TDR Impact Grants - South-East Asia (SEARO), Western Pacific (WPRO) and European (EURO) windows
funder: TDR with WHO regional offices (SEARO, WPRO, EURO)
amount: US$10,000-15,000 per grant (WPRO 2025-26 and EURO 2025: up to US$15,000)
countries: Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines
eligibility: PI must be based in an LMIC institution in the relevant WHO region: SEARO (India, Thailand), WPRO (Philippines, Viet Nam - both listed in the 2025-26 WPRO call), EURO (Armenia). Note Philippines and Viet Nam moved to upper-middle income in the World Bank FY27 classification (1 July 2026); they remain middle-income, but check each new call's country list. Prior IR experience and programme-manager endorsement typically required.
deadline: WPRO 2025-26 call closed 16 Jul 2025; EURO grants awarded May 2025 (36 applications, 10 awards); SEARO last awarded May 2024. No 2026-27 SEARO/WPRO/EURO call found as of 26 Sep 2026.
status_note: Expected/Uncertain - regional windows rotate; AFRO and PAHO 2026-27 calls ran in Jul-Sep 2026, so similar calls for other regions may follow.
what: Small implementation-research grants on infectious diseases of poverty tied to each region's priorities (e.g., WPRO 2025-26: reaching the unreached with a communicable-disease focus; EURO 2025: TB/HIV co-infection, parasitic infections, climate and vulnerable groups).
mechanisms: Impact Grants for Regional Priorities (regional calls managed by each WHO regional office; EURO implemented with Astana Medical University)
how: Register on eTDR, set alerts on tdr.who.int/grants and the regional office websites; prepare a 12-month routine-data IR protocol with programme endorsement.

name: ASTIF Call 2026 – ASEAN Grand Challenge: AI-Enabled Competitive and Resilient Region (Category 1: AI for Health, Bioeconomy and Food Security)
funder: ASEAN Science, Technology and Innovation Fund (ASEAN COSTI). Intergovernmental, not a philanthropy; included as a Grand Challenge-style call.
amount: Total budget US$1.2M; no fixed per-project cap. Salaries and stipends 30% or less on average.
countries: Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines
eligibility: Legally registered entities in ASEAN member states (universities, hospitals, NGOs, companies); individuals cannot apply. Teams must include members from at least two ASEAN countries. Not open to the other seven countries.
deadline: Submission window 1 Aug – 16 Oct 2026. Results 15 Feb 2027.
status_note: Open until 16 Oct 2026.
what: Collaborative AI projects across ASEAN countries, including AI for health.
mechanisms: ASTIF 2026 Grand Challenge call (Category 1 covers health).
how: Download the ASTIF 2026 announcement and standard template from astnet.asean.org/astif. Submit through your National COSTI Focal Point: Thailand MHESI, Vietnam MOST, Philippines DOST.

name: Global Health EDCTP3 Joint Undertaking — Work Programme 2026 calls
funder: European Union (Horizon Europe) with European and African participating states
amount: Varies by topic (often multi-million euro consortia)
countries: Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Consortia must include sub-Saharan African partners and typically European partners. African institutions can coordinate. Only the 3 African map countries fit the geographic scope. Uganda received 2026 emergency Ebola Bundibugyo research mobilisation funds (identified beneficiaries only).
deadline: DIGIT-02 and SERP-01 were listed as 'Open' in Sep 2026 — check exact deadlines on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal
status_note: Open (selected CSA topics) — most 2026 RIA topics closed
what: Clinical research and capacity building on infectious diseases in sub-Saharan Africa (HIV, TB, malaria, lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs), emerging infections, climate and health), including ethics/regulatory networks and digital/AI integration of research and care.
mechanisms: Research and Innovation Actions; Coordination and Support Actions (e.g., HORIZON-JU-GH-EDCTP3-2026-03-DIGIT-02 'Enhancing integrated research and healthcare in SSA through digital innovation and AI'; SERP-01 ethics/regulatory/pharmacovigilance training networks); outbreak research-fund mobilisation; EDCTP prizes
how: Search the topic IDs on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal. Use the EDCTP3 networking platform to find consortium partners.

name: Global Health EDCTP3 fellowships via training hubs (Strategic Training Hubs in epidemiology, biostatistics and modelling; career-development consortia)
funder: Global Health EDCTP3 with contributing partners and Africa CDC
amount: Up to EUR 90,000 per fellow (hub topic ceiling); hub grants up to EUR 1.25m
duration: Master's fellowships up to 24 months; other fellowships vary (e.g., CREATIVE 30 months)
countries: Uganda; Zimbabwe
eligibility: Fellows must be resident in, or willing to relocate to, a sub-Saharan EDCTP Association member country and not previously funded by a similar EDCTP fellowship; Master's fellows must be employed by the host and commit to 2 years after. Botswana residents generally not eligible (non-member).
deadline: Hub-specific calls; hubs from the 2025 topic expected to recruit fellows during 2026-2027.
status_note: Rolling/Expected - watch individual hub calls.
what: Fellowships awarded by EDCTP3-funded consortia: Master's fellowships in epidemiology/biostatistics, infectious-disease modelling training, and clinical-research career fellowships (e.g., CREATIVE at LSHTM partners, ACT-PREP).
mechanisms: Financial support to third parties (fellowships) through funded hubs; EDCTP3 no longer runs individual fellowship calls directly
how: Follow EDCTP3 and Africa CDC announcements and partner universities for hub fellowship calls; secure employer support letter.

name: Horizon Europe Cluster 1 Health - Work Programme 2026-2027
amount: Mostly EUR 1.5m-10m per project (consortium level)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Armenia is a Horizon Europe Associated Country (same status as EU members; can coordinate). Dominican Republic, Jamaica, Thailand, Philippines, Viet Nam, Uganda, Zimbabwe and Botswana are on the WP 2026-27 list of low- and middle-income countries automatically eligible for funding. India is NOT on the automatic list - Indian partners are funded only if a topic allows it or their participation is essential (India has some national co-funding arrangements). Consortium of 3+ entities from 3 EU/Associated countries usually required.
deadline: HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01 and 2027-02 open 29 Oct 2026, deadline 17 Feb 2027 (2027-02 stage 2: 16 Sep 2027); HORIZON-HLTH-2027-03 opens 3 Jun 2027, deadline 16 Sep 2027. 2026 calls closed (16 Apr and 15 Sep 2026).
status_note: Expected - next calls open 29 Oct 2026.
what: Collaborative research across six health destinations (e.g., infectious diseases, NCDs, health systems, digital health/AI, environment and health).
mechanisms: Research and Innovation Actions, Innovation Actions, CSAs (single- and two-stage)
how: EU Funding and Tenders Portal; register a PIC for your institution; contact national contact points (Armenia has NCPs) and European coordinators to join a consortium before Dec 2026.

name: Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) - Postdoctoral Fellowships and Staff Exchanges
amount: PF: unit-cost based living/mobility allowances (2026 call budget EUR 399m, ~1,600 fellowships); SE: unit cost per person-month of secondment
duration: PF 1-2 years (Global PF up to 3 years incl. return phase); SE secondments 1-12 months within 4-year projects
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: PF requires mobility to an EU/Associated-country host (Armenia is associated, so Armenian institutions can host). LMIC entities on the Horizon Europe list can join SE projects; India participates but is not automatically funded. Researchers of any nationality may apply for PF if they meet mobility rules and have a PhD.
deadline: PF 2026 closed 9 Sep 2026 (next PF call normally opens ~April 2027, closes ~September 2027). SE: 15 Dec 2026 - 15 Apr 2027 (verify on Portal).
status_note: Closed (PF) / Expected (Staff Exchanges opening Dec 2026).
what: Postdoctoral Fellowships (European or Global, any discipline) and Staff Exchanges that fund short secondments of staff between partner organisations, including with non-EU countries.
mechanisms: MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships (PF); MSCA Staff Exchanges (SE); Doctoral Networks
how: EU Funding and Tenders Portal; find a European supervisor (PF) or join an SE consortium led by an EU university partner.

name: Science for Africa Foundation (SFA Foundation) - DELTAS Africa II and other programmes

countries: Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana

name: IAEA Coordinated Research Projects (CRPs) - research contracts in radiation oncology, medical imaging, nuclear medicine and dosimetry
amount: Modest contract support (some CRPs state about EUR 3,000 per year per contract) plus IAEA-funded travel to Research Coordination Meetings

status_note: Rolling - new CRPs announced throughout 2026.

mechanisms: Research Contracts, Doctoral Contracts, Technical Contracts, Research Agreements (unfunded, for high-income institutes)
how: Browse iaea.org/projects/coordinated-research-projects and the Human Health Campus; email the proposal form to the Research Contracts Administration Section before the CRP deadline.

name: CEPI Calls for Proposals (epidemic/pandemic vaccines and enabling science)
amount: Varies widely (from targeted studies to multi-million vaccine awards)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Global applicants; CEPI states special interest in Global South developers and researchers. 2026 Bundibugyo calls sought epidemiology/modelling/analytics and immunological assessment of cross-reactive antibodies - directly relevant to Ugandan teams.

status_note: Rolling - CEPI raising funds for its next strategic period (e.g., US$240m new pledges Sept 2026); check for new calls.
what: Vaccine R&D, manufacturing, and enabling science including epidemiology, modelling, immunology and AI for priority pathogens and Disease X; outbreak-response calls (e.g., Bundibugyo virus in DRC and Uganda, 2026).
mechanisms: Open and rapid-response Calls for Proposals; CEPI Tech Talks (pre-application advice)
how: Monitor cepi.net/calls-for-proposals; request a CEPI Tech Talk by email to discuss fit before applying.

name: IAEA Technical Cooperation (TC) Programme - national/regional projects, fellowships and scientific visits
amount: In-kind (equipment, training, fellowships); varies by project
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: All Member States eligible, with focus on less developed countries. Access is via the National Liaison Officer (NLO) and national counterpart institutions - individuals are nominated through their government.
deadline: Project concepts are developed with the NLO for the next TC cycle; fellowship nominations tied to active projects.
status_note: Rolling (via national channels).
what: Capacity building where nuclear techniques add value: radiotherapy and nuclear medicine services, medical physics, diagnostic imaging QA, nutrition isotope techniques; delivered as equipment, expert missions, training courses, fellowships and scientific visits.
mechanisms: National, regional and interregional TC projects; fellowships/scientific visits attached to projects; capacity-building support to attend IAEA meetings
how: Contact your country's IAEA National Liaison Office (often the atomic energy/radiation authority) to join an existing health project or propose one for the next cycle.

name: ICGEB Research Grants - Collaborative Research Programme (CRP)
funder: International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (ICGEB)
amount: Up to EUR 25,000 per year (consumables, small equipment <EUR 10,000, training, limited travel); no PI salary or overheads
countries: Dominican Republic; India; Vietnam; Zimbabwe
eligibility: PI must hold a position at a university/research institute in an ICGEB Member State. Full members among the 10: India, Dominican Republic, Viet Nam, Zimbabwe. Armenia, Jamaica and Philippines are pending full membership and Thailand is only a signatory - not eligible until full membership. Botswana is not listed; Uganda is being engaged via the BiotechNet II project. Each country's Liaison Officer can endorse max 3 standard + 2 return-grant proposals.
deadline: 2026 round: submission 30 Apr 2026, national endorsement 31 May 2026 (closed). Next round expected with a similar April deadline in 2027.
status_note: Closed for 2026; Expected 2027.
what: Original research in basic life sciences, human healthcare and biotechnology addressing problems relevant to the host country, with a mandatory international collaboration and training component.
mechanisms: CRP Research Grants; CRP Early Career Return Grants (under 40, recently returned after 2+ years abroad); related ICGEB fellowships
how: ICGEB Service Gateway (isg.icgeb.org); contact your national ICGEB Liaison Officer early and line up an international collaborator with a letter.

name: UNICEF Venture Fund (frontier tech incl. AI for child health; Climate Ventures 2026)
amount: Up to US$100,000 equity-free
duration: About 12 months of support in cohort
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Applicant must be a for-profit startup registered in a UNICEF programme country (check the programme-country list), with a working prototype and commitment to open-source licensing. Women-led and young founders encouraged. Academic groups need a spin-out or startup partner.
deadline: Climate and health call closed 17 May 2026 (first of a five-year Climate Ventures programme); earlier health call closed Oct 2023. Further calls expected.
status_note: Closed/Expected - watch for the next Venture Fund call.
what: Equity-free investments in early-stage, open-source frontier-tech solutions (AI/ML, data science, blockchain, drones, XR) for children's health, nutrition, mental health and climate-health (early warning, disease forecasting, point-of-care triage, offline LLMs).
mechanisms: Thematic calls for applications; cohort support and mentorship
how: Follow unicef.org/innovation and unicefventurefund.org; prepare an open-source prototype and company registration.

name: Global Fund Grant Cycle 8 (2026-2028) country grants - operational research within national HIV/TB/malaria programmes
funder: The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria
amount: Varies; OR budgets are set within each country grant
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Eighth Replenishment closed at US$12.64bn; US$10.78bn allocated to countries (about 8% less than GC7). GC8 is the FINAL country allocation for: Armenia TB (Armenia HIV already ineligible); Botswana HIV and TB; Dominican Republic HIV; Jamaica HIV; Thailand HIV, TB and malaria; Viet Nam HIV and malaria; Philippines malaria; India HIV. deadline: GC8 funding requests and grant-making under way through 2026; grants run 2026-2028.
status_note: Open via country process - but budgets are tighter and more prioritised; transition countries have little room for new research.
what: Country grants to national programmes; operational research, program evaluation and surveys can be budgeted in grants (typically under M&E/RSSH), and PRs/sub-recipients sometimes contract local researchers.
mechanisms: Country allocations negotiated through Country Coordinating Mechanisms (CCMs); Principal/Sub-Recipient sub-grants; catalytic investments (US$260m)
how: Contact your national HIV/TB/malaria programme and the CCM secretariat; propose a costed, programme-priority OR question (e.g., case-finding, retention) for inclusion in grant work plans or PR sub-contracts.

name: Stop TB Partnership - TB REACH
funder: Stop TB Partnership (UNOPS-hosted); funded by Global Affairs Canada, UK FCDO and others
amount: Wave 11: up to US$550,000 per grant (28 projects, US$14.5m, 15 countries approved June 2024)
countries: India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe
eligibility: Wave-specific; past waves prioritised high TB-burden LMICs (listed countries are on WHO high-burden lists) and accepted NGOs, academic groups and public programmes. Confirm country eligibility in the next wave.
deadline: No open wave as of Sep 2026 (Wave 11 launched Nov 2023; Wave 11 Plus portfolio for NPOC tools under way).
status_note: Uncertain - next wave depends on donor funding.
what: Rapid, innovative projects to find and treat people with TB and test new delivery approaches (Wave 11: integrating TB and lung health at primary/community level; Wave 11 Plus: near-point-of-care TB tests in routine conditions), with independent M&E.
mechanisms: TB REACH waves of funding (competitive calls)
how: Monitor stoptb.org TB REACH pages and Union World Conference announcements (waves have been launched there); partner with national TB programme.

name: WHO headquarters, regional and country office commissioned research (APW/technical service agreements)
amount: Varies (usually small to mid-size contracts)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Usually institutional contracts; selection often via WHO country office networks. US withdrawal from WHO took effect in January 2026; WHO cut its 2026-27 programme budget by about a fifth to US$4.2 billion (from US$5.3 billion proposed) with a residual gap reported at about US$1.7 billion, so commissioned work is fewer and more targeted.
deadline: Ad hoc
status_note: Uncertain - reduced volume due to WHO budget cuts and restructuring.
what: Specific studies, evidence reviews, surveys and evaluations that WHO offices contract out to local institutions and researchers to inform guidelines and national programmes.
mechanisms: Agreements for Performance of Work (APW), requests for proposals, calls for experts
how: Introduce your unit to the WHO country office (NPO for your disease area), register interest in expert rosters, and monitor who.int calls for proposals and regional office pages.

name: WHO-hosted research partnerships: Alliance for Health Policy and Systems Research (AHPSR) and HRP (sexual and reproductive health research)
amount: Varies by call (not stated)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Usually institutional applicants in LMICs; calls often restricted to specific countries/themes. HRP's research impact grants page is no longer updated.
deadline: Ad hoc; no open call found as of Sep 2026.
status_note: Uncertain - no open calls identified; HRP running a 2026-2036 SRHR research prioritisation.
what: AHPSR commissions health policy and systems research through targeted requests for proposals; HRP supports SRHR research and research-capacity strengthening through its HRP Alliance hubs and ad-hoc small grants.
mechanisms: AHPSR requests for proposals; HRP Alliance research capacity strengthening (new RCS strategy launched 2026); ad-hoc small grants (historically for emergencies, e.g., Zika, migrant SRH)
how: Check ahpsr.who.int calls-for-proposals and the HRP pages; sign up to newsletters; connect with the regional HRP Alliance hub.

name: The Pandemic Fund - Fourth Call for Proposals
funder: The Pandemic Fund (World Bank-hosted financial intermediary fund)
amount: Up to US$244m total across 15 countries (country-specific ceilings)
countries: Uganda
eligibility: Only 15 high-risk, high-need countries that have not had single-country grants are eligible; Uganda is the only one among the 10. Applicants are governments with implementing entities, not individuals. Third round (Feb 2026) awarded US$499.6m to 20 projects.
deadline: Rolling: 1 Apr 2026 - 31 Mar 2027
status_note: Open (Uganda only).
what: Government-led investments in disease surveillance, laboratory systems and health workforce for pandemic prevention, preparedness and response.
mechanisms: Fourth CfP with pre-set country ceilings; rolling applications through accredited Implementing Entities (WHO, UNICEF, FAO, MDBs etc.)
how: Ugandan researchers should contact the MoH/National Public Health Institute team preparing the proposal to embed surveillance/lab/workforce evaluation components.

name: Unitaid Calls for Proposals
amount: Multi-million US$ (e.g., US$30m envelope for the 2026 cervical cancer call)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Applicants are consortia with strong implementation and financial capacity; implementation countries are LMICs chosen per call. Local clinicians join as country partners/sub-grantees rather than lead applicants.
deadline: 2026 calls closed (integrated diagnostics 29 Jan 2026; INSPIRE MNH supply chains 20 Mar 2026; cervical cancer 9 Apr 2026). No open calls as of Sep 2026.
status_note: Closed - no open calls; new calls appear several times a year.
what: Large, time-bound projects that introduce and scale innovative health products and delivery models (diagnostics integration, cervical cancer secondary prevention, maternal/newborn supply chains, heat stability of products, lenacapavir PrEP rollout).
mechanisms: Thematic calls for proposals to implementation consortia
how: Monitor unitaid.org/calls-for-proposals; approach lead consortia (NGOs, academic partners) to be named as a country implementation site.

name: Dissemination and Implementation Research in Health — R03 (PAR-25-233) and R21 (PAR-25-143)
funder: US NIH (multi-institute; Fogarty is a partner)
amount: NIH standard: R03 up to US$50,000/yr direct for 2 yrs; R21 up to US$275,000 direct over 2 yrs (confirm in each NOFO)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Check Section III of each NOFO to see whether non-US (foreign) organizations may apply directly; many NIH research grant NOFOs allow this. If the lead is US with an LMIC partner, the partner must now be structured as a linked RF2 award under PF5, not a subaward.
deadline: Multiple standard due dates per NOFO (see announcements)
status_note: Open (listed in Fogarty's Aug 2026 newsletter)
what: Small and exploratory studies on how to spread, adopt, implement and sustain evidence-based health interventions in real-world clinical and public-health settings.
mechanisms: R03 small grant (clinical trial not allowed); R21 exploratory (clinical trial optional)
how: Read PAR-25-233 / PAR-25-143 on grants.nih.gov. Confirm foreign eligibility and register in SAM.gov, Grants.gov and eRA Commons.

name: Emerging Global Leader Award (K43) — PAR-24-295 (clinical trial required) / PAR-24-296 (clinical trial not allowed)
funder: US National Institutes of Health — Fogarty International Center (FIC)
amount: Up to US$100,000/yr salary (minimum 75% effort) + up to US$40,000/yr research development support, plus fringe
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: The applicant organization must be an academic or research institution in an LMIC (World Bank low, lower-middle and upper-middle income all count). The LMIC institution applies directly; no US prime institution is needed, but a US mentor is normally part of the team. The candidate must commit at least 75% effort, which is hard for full-time clinicians unless protected time can be negotiated. Fogarty excludes G20 upper-middle-income countries (Argentina, Brazil, China, Indonesia, Mexico, South Africa, Turkey) from its research-training programmes. None of the 10 map countries is affected (India is G20 but lower-middle income). Foreign applicants need SAM.gov (with an NCAGE code), Grants.gov and eRA Commons registrations, which take weeks.
deadline: Annual. Last receipt date under current NOFOs is 3 December 2026 (NOFOs expire 4 Dec 2026). Review Mar 2027, earliest start Jul 2027.
status_note: Open — Fogarty's ONLY own open NOFO as of Sep 2026. Reissue after Dec 2026 is uncertain: the FY2027 President's Budget proposes eliminating Fogarty, while the House FY2027 Labor-HHS bill keeps it at US$95M (the FY2026 level).
what: Mentored research career-development award for early-career scientists holding a faculty or research post at an LMIC institution. Covers salary plus research costs so the awardee can build an independent research program at home.
mechanisms: K43 career development award (two NOFOs: independent clinical trial required / not allowed)
how: Start SAM.gov/NCAGE, Grants.gov and eRA Commons registration NOW (it takes weeks). Identify a US mentor plus a home-institution mentor. Submit through Grants.gov/ASSIST by 3 Dec 2026, 5 pm local time.

name: AREF–MRC Towards Leadership Programme
funder: Africa Research Excellence Fund (AREF) with UKRI Medical Research Council
amount: Not stated (training programme, not a cash grant)
countries: Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: For emerging scientists based in Africa.
deadline: 2026/27 application deadline 28 Aug 2026
status_note: Closed for 2026/27; expected to recur
what: A leadership-development programme (not a research grant) for emerging African health researchers: research leadership, grant writing, team building and international collaboration.
mechanisms: Cohort-based training programme
how: Check the AREF funding-calls page for the next cohort.

name: Academy of Medical Sciences Networking Grants (ISPF-funded)
funder: Academy of Medical Sciences, with the UK National Academies; funded by the International Science Partnerships Fund (ISPF)
amount: Up to £25,000 (up to £20k travel/events/admin; up to £5k consumables for pilot data; no salaries)
countries: India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda
eligibility: The LEAD applicant must be based OUTSIDE the UK in an eligible country, with one UK co-applicant. Both need a PhD or equivalent experience and a permanent post or a contract covering the grant period. Uganda qualifies as an LDC. The Dominican Republic, Jamaica, Armenia, Zimbabwe and Botswana are not on the lists.
deadline: Next round dates to be confirmed
status_note: Expected — scheme live but round dates TBC; depends on continued ISPF ODA funding
what: Small grants for networking and collaboration between an overseas lead researcher and a UK co-applicant: workshops, travel and pilot data.
mechanisms: Networking grant. Stream 1 covers 'developed' partner countries and includes India. Stream 2 covers DAC-listed ISPF countries: Brazil, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Kenya, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand, Turkey, South Africa, Vietnam, plus all UN Least Developed Countries.
how: Find a UK co-applicant now. Register on the AMS Flexi-Grant portal and watch the scheme page for round dates.

name: NIHR Global Advanced Fellowship (and NIHR Global Research Professorship)
amount: Not stated here — see the NIHR guidance
countries: India; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: The applicant must hold a PhD and be based at an institution in an eligible sub-Saharan African or South Asian ODA country; LMIC-based researchers lead. Other map countries are ineligible from 2026.
deadline: The 2026 round closed 30 Jun 2026
status_note: Closed (2026 round). Expected — NIHR has run it as a recurring call.
what: Postdoctoral fellowships for researchers based in eligible LMICs to lead applied global health research, training and capacity strengthening. From 2026 the focus is on infectious diseases of poverty in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. The Global Research Professorship is a senior-leadership equivalent.
mechanisms: Personal fellowship (Global Advanced Fellowship, Cohort 2); Global Research Professorship
how: Read the Global Advanced Fellowship eligibility and 'how to apply' pages. Secure a host institution and mentors now for the next round.

name: ANRS Emerging Infectious Diseases (ANRS MIE, Inserm) — calls for projects and South partner-site network
funder: ANRS MIE (autonomous agency of Inserm), France
amount: Varies by call
countries: Vietnam
eligibility: Calls are open to French research teams. Foreign teams are eligible for some calls when associated with a French laboratory. ANRS MIE partner sites are mostly in francophone Africa and Southeast Asia; Vietnam has historically been a site (verify).
deadline: Conferences & Publications 2027-1 call: 1 Sep – 15 Dec 2026; generic calls twice yearly
status_note: Open (Conferences & Publications); generic calls recurring
what: Research on HIV/AIDS, viral hepatitis, STIs, TB and emerging infections, including in resource-limited countries through its international partner-site network. Also doctoral/postdoc grants, mobility, conferences and publications.
mechanisms: Two generic calls per year plus thematic calls; Conferences & Publications call; Start programme for young researchers
how: Partner with a French lab. Apply via the Apogée platform.

name: Advancing Global Health Annual Program Statement (APS) — GHSD
funder: US Department of State — Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy
amount: Up to US$4.5 billion total ceiling across all awards; per-award amounts are in the country calls
countries: Dominican Republic; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Botswana
eligibility: Open to US and FOREIGN private organizations, higher-education institutions and faith-based organizations. Targets MOU countries (the first calls were Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire and Mozambique, due 15 Sep 2026). Map-country calls had not been confirmed as of Sep 2026.
deadline: Rolling country calls (the APS was amended 18 Aug 2026)
status_note: Open — umbrella APS active; watch for calls covering map countries
what: Awards to organizations that 'complement, extend and/or fill identified gaps' in implementing the bilateral health MOUs. It is issued as country-specific calls under an umbrella APS.
mechanisms: Annual Program Statement with country addenda (grants/cooperative agreements)
how: Search Grants.gov for the APS (DFOP0017890). Register in SAM.gov. Monitor country addenda for Uganda, Dominican Republic, Botswana, Philippines and Vietnam.

name: CDC Global Health Center — country office cooperative agreements
funder: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
amount: FY2027 request US$663.8m for the Center for Global Health (flat); the House FY2027 bill funds CDC global health at US$693m and consolidates HIV/TB/vaccines into a new 'Global Emerging Infectious Diseases' line (US$190.6m)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Most awards go to governments and national public-health institutes. Universities and NGOs can apply when a NOFO allows. The countries listed are those historically with CDC presence; confirm current country offices.
deadline: Per NOFO
status_note: Open but shrinking/restructuring — CDC is being repositioned to 'replace functions of the WHO' under America First
what: Global health security, polio and measles, HIV/TB and field epidemiology (FETP) support, mainly through cooperative agreements with ministries of health, public-health institutes and universities.
mechanisms: Cooperative-agreement NOFOs on Grants.gov; FETP training
how: Search Grants.gov for CDC-GH NOFOs naming your country. Contact the CDC country office (if present) and join FETP-linked research.

name: Global-health funding across other NIH Institutes (e.g., NIAID, NCI Center for Global Health, NIMH, NHLBI) via investigator-initiated R01/R21 and specialized NOFOs
funder: US National Institutes of Health (various ICs)
amount: Varies
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Foreign institutions may apply to NOFOs that allow non-domestic entities, and must justify why the work needs the foreign setting. NIH removed separate AIDS application due dates from NOFOs in Jan 2026 (NOT-OD-26-029). NIH's FY2027 request proposes an overall cut of about US$5 billion.
deadline: NIH standard due dates (Feb/Jun/Oct cycles) or per NOFO
status_note: Open but constrained — a funding squeeze and policy changes are in progress
what: Investigator-initiated and targeted research on HIV, TB, malaria, cancer, mental health, cardiometabolic disease and other conditions, including studies at LMIC sites.
mechanisms: Parent R01/R21/R03, PF5 international parent, specialized NOFOs; administrative supplements to active grants (PA-26-001)
how: Use Fogarty's 'NIH Global Health Funding' page and NIH RePORTER to find ICs funding your topic. Partnering with an existing NIH grantee (e.g., via an administrative supplement) is the realistic entry point.

name: IDRC (International Development Research Centre) — Global Health programme and competitive calls
amount: Varies by call
countries: India; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Southern institutions usually lead directly (no Canadian partner needed in many calls). Recent calls were Africa-focused. Canada announced CA$2.7bn in ODA cuts over 4 years (Nov 2025): IDRC loses CA$11m from FY2026/27, rising to CA$24m/yr.
deadline: Only open call as of Sep 2026: SGCI/STISA-2034 multilateral research call (EOI deadline 25 Sep 2026). ANeSA letters of interest closed 23 Aug 2026.
status_note: Open (limited) — few health-specific calls; budget shrinking
what: Research by Global South institutions on health systems, sexual and reproductive health, climate and health, and AI. Mostly through targeted calls and co-funded initiatives (e.g., the SGCI Science Granting Councils Initiative in sub-Saharan Africa, ANeSA on neglected SRHR areas in sub-Saharan Africa).
mechanisms: Competitive calls (letters of interest, concept notes, full proposals); co-funded partnerships
how: Subscribe to IDRC funding alerts at idrc-crdi.ca/en/funding. Apply through the call-specific portal.

name: Digital Health Technology and Reciprocal Innovation program (relaunch of Fogarty mHealth R21/R33)
amount: Not stated (concept only)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: The concept stresses US–LMIC collaboration. Final eligibility will be in the NOFO. A US lead would require the PF5/RF2 structure.
deadline: No NOFO yet
status_note: Expected — concept presented to the Fogarty Advisory Board in June 2026. Clearance does not guarantee a NOFO, and Fogarty's FY2027 budget is contested.
what: Proposed program for developing, validating, implementing and evaluating digital health tools — mHealth, AI/ML, digital diagnostics, telehealth, clinical decision support — for low-resource settings in LMICs and underserved US settings, with bidirectional US–LMIC learning.
mechanisms: Expected exploratory/developmental and phased mechanisms (the previous mHealth program used R21 and R21/R33)
how: Subscribe to Fogarty's funding newsletter. Line up a US digital-health collaborator and pilot data now.

name: Fogarty Research Training Programs (D43) — Global Infectious Disease, HIV, NCD-LIFESPAN, Bioethics, Research Administration, LAUNCH
amount: Varies by NOFO (typically a few hundred thousand US$/yr total costs) — see each NOFO
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Historically either an LMIC institution or a US institution partnered with LMIC institutions could apply. G20 upper-middle-income countries (Argentina, Brazil, China, Indonesia, Mexico, South Africa, Turkey) are excluded, and for NOFOs published after 8 Aug 2026 there is no longer an exception for Sub-Saharan African G20 UMICs. US-led versions now must use the new PF5/RF2 foreign-collaboration structure. Individual clinicians benefit as TRAINEES of an existing D43 at their institution, not as applicants.
deadline: No D43 due dates listed on Fogarty's deadline page as of Sep 2026. LAUNCH D43 (RFA-TW-25-002) had an estimated due date of 25 May 2026.
status_note: Expected / Uncertain — the Fogarty Advisory Board cleared concepts for reissue (Infectious Disease D43, Bioethics and LAUNCH in Sep 2025; HIV D43, NCD-LIFESPAN D43 and Research Administration in Sep 2024), but no new NOFOs had been posted as of Sep 2026. Fogarty's survival in FY2027 depends on Congress.
what: Institutional research-training grants that build a cadre of LMIC researchers through degree and non-degree training, mentoring and small research projects. Topics include infectious diseases, HIV, chronic NCDs across the lifespan, bioethics and research administration.
mechanisms: D43 institutional training grants (several thematic NOFOs); LAUNCH D43 (RFA-TW-25-002)
how: Check whether your institution or a regional partner already holds a Fogarty D43 (search Fogarty's grants database) and apply as a trainee. Institutions should watch Fogarty's weekly funding newsletter for reissued NOFOs.

name: GACD 11th joint call — CIHR Team Grant 'Implementation science to tackle NCDs: maximizing collaboration with and beyond the healthcare system'
funder: Canadian Institutes of Health Research (IPPH, ICRH) as part of the Global Alliance for Chronic Diseases (GACD) multi-funder call
amount: CIHR: up to CA$200,000/yr, max CA$1,000,000 per grant; about CA$3M total (about 3 grants)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: LMIC is defined by the World Bank, so all 10 map countries qualify as research settings. CIHR funds the Canadian side, which needs a Canadian nominated PI. LMIC teams are typically funded by their own GACD member agency, if their country has one, or through the Canadian grant. Stage 1 has passed.
deadline: Stage 1 June 2026 (passed); Stage 2 late Oct/early Nov 2026 (invited only); funding starts Jan 2027
status_note: Closed to new entrants (in Stage 2). Expected — GACD runs recurring joint calls.
what: Implementation research on NCD prevention, screening and continuity of care, using settings and sectors beyond the formal health system (communities, NGOs, faith-based groups) in LMICs and underserved high-income-country populations.
mechanisms: CIHR Team Grant (IPPH and ICRH pools). Other GACD member agencies fund their own national components (see gacd.org).
how: Use the GACD collaborator forum to find partners for the next call. Check whether your country's research council is a GACD member.

name: Grand Challenges Canada — Nexa (climate × health), Nexa Lighthouse (Asia-Pacific), Being (youth mental health); former Stars in Global Health
funder: Grand Challenges Canada (funded by Global Affairs Canada)
amount: Varies by RFP
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Eligible countries are defined per call. The 2026 Nexa call covered Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean (so Uganda, Zimbabwe, Botswana, DR and Jamaica could qualify). Being covered 12 countries including India and Vietnam. Nexa Lighthouse (with AVPN) targets Asia-Pacific.
deadline: No open opportunities as of Aug–Sep 2026. Nexa Proof of Concept closed 22 Jul 2026; Transition to Scale closed 12 Aug 2026; Being closed 31 Mar 2026.
status_note: Closed — Nexa Lighthouse (Asia-Pacific climate-health) launching; watch for a call
what: Innovation grants for 'bold ideas with big impact': Proof of Concept and Transition to Scale funding for locally led health innovations. The 2026 calls covered climate-driven health risks and youth mental health.
mechanisms: Proof of Concept; Transition to Scale; thematic RFPs (the former open 'Stars in Global Health' has been replaced by thematic calls)
how: Sign up for the GCC newsletter. Applications go through the Fluxx portal (gcc.fluxx.io) when a call opens; unsolicited proposals are not accepted.

name: NIHR Global Health Research (GHR) Themed Programme 2026 — Tackling bacterial and fungal antimicrobial resistance in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia
funder: UK National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), Department of Health and Social Care ODA
amount: £500,000–£5m overall; Band 3 £500,000–£1.5m (10–20% for capacity strengthening)
duration: Band 3 up to 3 years; larger bands longer
countries: India; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: From 2026 NIHR global health funding is restricted to ODA-eligible countries in SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA and SOUTH ASIA. The Dominican Republic, Jamaica, Armenia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines are therefore out of scope for new NIHR calls. LMIC institutions can lead (Band 3 explicitly allows a sole LMIC lead). The UK cut ODA to 0.3% of GNI by 2027, which drove the narrowing.
deadline: Outline stage closed 8 Jul 2026; full applications (invited only) close Dec 2026. The next annual theme is expected in 2027.
status_note: Closed to new outlines (2026). Expected — a new theme is advertised each year.
what: Applied health research — including later-stage trials and implementation research — on antimicrobial stewardship, preventing AMR infections and improving AMR-related outcomes for WHO-priority bacterial and fungal pathogens. The theme will change each year under a new global-health-security focus.
mechanisms: Researcher-led, 2-stage call in three bands. Band 3 is for new or early-career-led teams or single-setting projects and can be led by a sole LMIC lead applicant or jointly. Bands 1–2 are for larger programmes up to £5m.
how: Watch the NIHR GHR Themed Programme page for the 2027 theme. Build an AMR/global-health-security team with a UK or regional partner. Apply through the NIHR Research Management System.

name: Research Council of Norway — Researcher Project for Early Career Scientists on Global Health and Development Research (+ Pre-projects on Global Health)
funder: Research Council of Norway (Forskningsrådet), with Norad/Ministry of Foreign Affairs ODA
amount: NOK 4–10 million per project (NOK 120m pot in 2026); pre-projects up to NOK 250,000
countries: India; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe
eligibility: The Project Owner must be an approved NORWEGIAN research organisation, and the project manager must have defended a PhD between 11 Mar 2019 and 1 Jun 2024. Partners from LDC/LIC/LMIC countries on the DAC list are REQUIRED, with joint scientific leadership and a fair share of funds. Upper-middle-income partners (DR, Jamaica, Armenia, Thailand, Botswana) can join but share at most 20% of funding with high-income partners.
deadline: 2026 call closed 27 May 2026 (projects start Mar–Dec 2027)
status_note: Closed (2026). Expected — recurring call.
what: Early-career-led research on health inequalities, health security, poverty and development, with equitable joint leadership by partners in low- and lower-middle-income countries. Pre-project grants fund partnership building and proposal writing.
mechanisms: Researcher Project for Early Career Scientists; Pre-projects on Global Health (up to NOK 250,000)
how: Find a Norwegian early-career partner (the University of Bergen, University of Oslo and NTNU all run global health groups). Apply for a pre-project to co-develop the proposal.

name: Solution-oriented Research for Development (SOR4D) — Phase 2 (2026–2031)
funder: Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) and Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC)
amount: CHF 22.4 million total for Phase 2 (per-project amount in the call document)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Open to ODA-eligible (OECD DAC list) countries. A Swiss research partner AND a non-academic practice partner (government, civil society or private) in the ODA country are required.
deadline: Pre-proposals closed 18 May 2026
status_note: Closed (2026 pre-proposal round); Phase 2 runs to 2031, so further calls are possible
what: Transdisciplinary, solution-oriented research by mixed consortia (Swiss researchers + ODA-country researchers + non-academic practice partners) on the SDGs, including human development and health.
mechanisms: Two-stage (pre-proposal, then full proposal) consortium grants; Transformation Accelerating Grants (12–24 months extra for scaling)
how: Build a Swiss partnership (e.g., Swiss TPH, University of Bern). Monitor sor4d.ch and the SNSF 'Open calls' page; submit via mySNF.

name: AI4D Africa (Artificial Intelligence for Development)
amount: Varies by call
countries: Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Africa only; calls are issued through AI4D partner hubs.
deadline: Per call
status_note: Uncertain — check ai4d.ai for open calls
what: African AI capacity: PhD and postdoc fellowships, innovation and policy research networks, and university AI labs — including responsible AI for health.
mechanisms: Fellowships; network and lab grants run by African partner hubs
how: Monitor ai4d.ai and IDRC alerts.

name: Australia — NHMRC (incl. GACD participation) and DFAT 'Partnerships for a Healthy Region'
funder: National Health and Medical Research Council; Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
amount: Varies
countries: Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines
eligibility: NHMRC requires an Australian-based chief investigator. DFAT's regional focus fits the Southeast Asian map countries.
deadline: NHMRC annual scheme calendar
status_note: Uncertain — not verified for 2026
what: NHMRC funds Australian-led research, including international collaborations and GACD calls. DFAT funds health-security and health-system programmes in Southeast Asia and the Pacific (not open research grants).
mechanisms: NHMRC Investigator/Ideas/Synergy grants and international schemes; DFAT programme partnerships
how: Partner with Australian institutions (e.g., the Burnet Institute, Kirby Institute or George Institute) that have Southeast Asian programmes.

name: Belgium — VLIR-UOS university cooperation and ITM–DGD framework programme
funder: VLIR-UOS; Institute of Tropical Medicine Antwerp (ITM) with Belgian Development Cooperation (DGD)
amount: Varies
countries: Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda

Flemish university partners are required for projects. ITM scholarships for its master's in public health and tropical medicine are open to LMIC health professionals.
deadline: Per call
status_note: Uncertain — not verified for 2026
what: Institutional university cooperation, joint research projects, scholarships (master's and PhD) and ITM's capacity-strengthening partnerships in tropical medicine and public health.
mechanisms: Calls for projects and scholarships; ITM institutional partnerships
how: Check vliruos.be/en/calls and ITM's scholarship pages.

name: Germany — BMFTR (formerly BMBF) global health programmes, DFG international cooperation, DAAD scholarships, Else Kröner-Fresenius-Stiftung, GIZ
funder: BMFTR (Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space); DFG; DAAD; Else Kröner-Fresenius-Stiftung (private foundation); GIZ
amount: Varies
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: BMFTR and DFG normally require a German-based lead applicant. DAAD offers individual scholarships to LMIC researchers. Germany has cut its development and humanitarian budgets since 2024 (verify 2026 levels). No specific 2026 health call was verified in this review.
deadline: Per programme
status_note: Uncertain — not verified for 2026
what: BMFTR: research networks and product development for neglected and poverty-related diseases, mainly with African partners. DFG: bilateral cooperation and 'initiation of international collaboration' for German-based researchers. DAAD: scholarships and research stays for scientists from developing countries. EKFS (private): medical research partnerships, historically including LMIC clinical research. GIZ: implementation, not research grants.
mechanisms: Programme calls (BMFTR); DFG individual grants with international components; DAAD scholarships; EKFS grant programmes
how: LMIC clinicians: search the DAAD scholarship database for research stays. Find German partners for DFG/BMFTR calls.

name: Global Brain and Nervous System Disorders Research Across the Lifespan (R21 exploratory / R01)
funder: US NIH — Fogarty International Center with partner NIH institutes
amount: R21: NIH standard is up to US$275,000 direct over 2 years (confirm in the NOFO); R01 larger
duration: R21 up to 2 yrs; R01 up to 5 yrs
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Historically required a US–LMIC collaboration, with LMIC institutions able to apply directly or as a foreign component. A US-led application with an LMIC partner must now use the PF5/RF2 structure (the LMIC partner receives its own linked RF2 award).
deadline: PAR-25-456 had an estimated due date of 24 Feb 2026; later dates not confirmed
status_note: Uncertain — not listed on Fogarty's deadline page as of Sep 2026
what: Collaborative research on nervous-system development, function and disorders (neurological, mental health, substance use) relevant to LMICs across the life course.
mechanisms: R21 exploratory/developmental (PAR-25-456); R01
how: Read PAR-25-456 on grants.nih.gov for remaining due dates. Contact the Fogarty program officer before preparing a proposal.

name: Korea — KOICA and KOFIH (Korea Foundation for International Healthcare) health programmes and fellowships
funder: Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA); Korea Foundation for International Healthcare (KOFIH, Ministry of Health and Welfare)
amount: Not stated (in-kind training costs)
countries: Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda
eligibility: Partner-country lists vary; historically these include Vietnam, the Philippines and several African countries such as Uganda (verify the current list). Candidates are usually nominated through the Ministry of Health.
deadline: Not verified
status_note: Uncertain
what: Bilateral health-system projects and health-workforce training. KOFIH runs fellowships and training for health professionals from partner countries (e.g., the HW Lee Jong-wook fellowship).
mechanisms: Fellowships and training in Korea; bilateral projects
how: Ask your Ministry of Health or the KOICA country office about nominations.

name: SATREPS — Science and Technology Research Partnership for Sustainable Development (infectious-disease track run by AMED)
funder: Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development (AMED) / Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST), with JICA
amount: Not stated here (multi-year, per-project budgets in the call)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Requires a JAPANESE principal investigator AND a matching government-to-government ODA request, so planning takes more than a year. All ODA-eligible countries can in principle take part.
deadline: Annual (autumn call is typical) — not verified for FY2027
status_note: Uncertain — not verified

amount: From a few lakh rupees to a few tens of crores
countries: India

status_note: Rolling

mechanisms: Organisational/programme grants (online 'Apply for a Grant')
how: Use 'Apply for a Grant' on azimpremjifoundation.org; best via a partner NGO for community health projects with evaluation.

funder: Draper Richards Kaplan Foundation (venture-philanthropy, VC founders)

countries: India; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana

status_note: Rolling — open

mechanisms: Unrestricted grant or investment plus DRK board seat and capacity support
how: Online application (30–60 min) at drkfoundation.org/apply; ~8–10 weeks initial review.

name: GiveWell grants — RFIs/RFPs and direct inquiries
amount: Not fixed — from small research grants to very large program grants (2026 grantmaking expected near US$1bn)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Organisations, not individuals. No formal application process — email research@givewell.org. 2026 RFIs were geographically narrow: vaccination outreach only in DRC/Nigeria/Somalia; iron programs anywhere in Africa except high-malaria countries (Uganda excluded; Zimbabwe and Botswana eligible); malaria pilots/research in Africa.
deadline: 2026 RFIs closed (vaccination and anemia 27 Mar 2026; malaria extended to 3 Jul 2026)
status_note: Rolling (email inquiries only) — no RFI open as of Sept 2026
what: Highly cost-effective programs and research in malaria, vaccines, nutrition/anemia, water, livelihoods and 'new areas' (e.g. medicine supply chains, oxygen devices, newborn care studies in India).
mechanisms: Organisational grants; periodic public RFIs/RFPs; research/evaluation funding
how: Review prioritized program list and past grants, then email research@givewell.org; watch GiveWell blog for new RFIs.

name: Novo Nordisk Foundation – global health funding (unsolicited EOI and partnership calls)
amount: Unsolicited: not stated. The EDCTP3 partnership totals up to EUR 18M.
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: No geographic restriction is stated for unsolicited EOIs; NNF has offices in Nairobi and New Delhi. Excluded: individual endeavours, travel or training salaries, general operations, construction, conference sponsorship, and resubmissions of projects rejected in open calls. Most NNF open-competition calls are Nordic-focused. Nexa covered Africa only (Uganda, Zimbabwe, Botswana). EDCTP3 calls favour sub-Saharan members (Uganda and Zimbabwe are members; Armenia as a Horizon Europe associated country only within a consortium).
deadline: Unsolicited EOI: rolling. No LMIC-focused open-competition call open as of 28 Sep 2026.
status_note: Rolling (unsolicited EOI). The Nexa Africa heat call and EVAH closed in 2026. The EDCTP3 2027 work-programme calls are not yet published.
what: Health, life-science and global-health projects. For LMIC applicants the main routes are the rolling unsolicited Expression of Interest, co-funded calls (EVAH on AI, Nexa on heat and cardiometabolic disease in Africa) and a partnership with Global Health EDCTP3.
mechanisms: Unsolicited Expression of Interest or unsolicited application via the NORMA portal (rolling). Co-funded calls: Nexa heat/cardiometabolic Africa (closed 22 Jul 2026), EVAH (closed). Global Health EDCTP3 partnership (up to EUR 18M across the 2026–27 work programmes).
how: Create a profile on NORMA (norma.novonordiskfonden.dk). Submit a short EOI: applicant, institution, brief project description, approximate amount. NNF says this route is not a fast track.

name: Science and Global Health R&D Fund — unsolicited proposal form
amount: Not published (varies widely)
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: No geographic restriction stated; historically only ~1–2% of unsolicited proposals funded. Only good-fit submissions receive a response.
deadline: None — rolling
status_note: Rolling — form open Sept 2026
what: Neglected, high-DALY biomedical and global-health R&D (vaccines, diagnostics, therapeutics, market shaping, e.g. malaria vaccine trials, sickle-cell diagnostics, protein design). Unlikely to fund cancer, diabetes, reproductive medicine, rare diseases, pain, mental health or most HIV work.
mechanisms: Grants and occasional investments; mostly proactive outreach, but an unsolicited proposal form is read.
how: Submit a short idea via the Airtable proposal form linked from the Funding Criteria page.

name: Wellcome Career Development Awards
amount: Resources as justified. Annual expenditure is usually below £250,000 excluding the applicant's salary; higher requests get extra scrutiny.
countries: Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Current rule: host in the UK, Ireland or an LMIC other than India and mainland China. From 29 Oct 2026: UK plus LMICs in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia only. Dominican Republic, Jamaica and Armenia qualify only if submitted by 28 Oct 2026. India is not eligible (use the India Alliance).
deadline: No deadline; apply anytime (open since 25 Aug 2026). Shortlisting Feb, Jun and Sep; interviews May, Sep and Jan.
status_note: Rolling. Apply-anytime model since 25 Aug 2026; location rule narrows 29 Oct 2026.
what: Mid-career researchers with a track record who want to lead an ambitious research programme and establish themselves as research leaders.
mechanisms: Career Development Award.
how: Check eligibility on the scheme page. Agree the resources your organisation will provide. Submit on funding.wellcome.org.

name: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme
amount: Tuition and living expenses; 50% grant and 50% loan.
countries: India; Uganda
eligibility: Nationals of listed countries only; India and Uganda are listed, the other eight are not. Priority to applicants under 30. Aga Khan University's internal research grants are for AKU faculty and students only.
deadline: 2026–27 cycle closed. Next cycle opens early 2027.
status_note: Expected, opening early 2027.
what: Postgraduate study (mainly master's) for outstanding students from selected developing countries with no other means of financing. Public health and medicine are eligible fields.
mechanisms: Scholarship (50% grant / 50% loan).
how: Get the form from the AKF office or local contact in India or Uganda when the cycle opens.

name: Bloomberg Initiative to Reduce Tobacco Use – Tobacco Control Grants Program (and Cessation Grants)
funder: Bloomberg Philanthropies (administered by Vital Strategies and Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids)
amount: Tobacco control: US$25,000–250,000 per year. Cessation: up to US$400,000.
duration: Short-term, 1-year or 2-year projects. Cessation up to 24 months.
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Government bodies, NGOs with policy-advocacy experience, universities and think tanks. The Open round covers all low- and middle-income countries, which includes all 10. The Strategic round covers priority countries only (India, Vietnam and the Philippines among the 10). Research and academic studies are not eligible, so a clinician needs a policy or advocacy angle.
deadline: Round 40 and Cessation Round 7 Project Idea windows are closed; outcome notices were due by 25 Sep 2026. Next round date not stated.
status_note: Closed; next round expected but no date published.
what: Policy-change projects on MPOWER measures (tax, smoke-free laws, advertising bans, graphic warnings, FCTC Article 5.3). Separate cessation grants cover brief advice in primary care, quitlines and mobile cessation. It does not fund research, surveys or individuals.
mechanisms: Open Grant Round (any LMIC). Strategic Grant Round (priority countries only). Cessation Grants Program.
how: Sign up for round alerts at tobaccocontrolgrants.org. When a round opens, submit a short Project Idea online in English; shortlisted applicants are invited to write a full proposal.

name: Evidence for AI in Health (EVAH) RFP
funder: Gates Foundation, Wellcome, Novo Nordisk Foundation (delivered by J-PAL and APHRC)
amount: Pathway A up to US$1,000,000. Pathway B up to US$3,000,000. The joint initiative totals US$60M.
countries: India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Lead institutions must be based in sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia or South-East Asia. Dominican Republic, Jamaica and Armenia are out of region. Applicants may be nonprofits, companies, universities, government agencies or consortia, and need access to an AI tool already deployed or deployment-ready. Selected proposals move to one of the three funders for due diligence, so each funder's own rules may apply (e.g., Wellcome does not fund India directly).
deadline: Spring 2026 round closed 1 Apr 2026. Next round not stated.
status_note: Closed. Decisions on the first round were going out mid-2026. No second RFP announced.
what: Locally led evaluations of AI-enabled clinical decision-support tools (triage, diagnosis, referral) used by frontline workers in primary and community care. Tools must already be deployed or ready for deployment.
mechanisms: Pathway A: real-world evaluation of tools early in deployment. Pathway B: rigorous impact evaluation of tools ready for scale.
how: Watch the J-PAL EVAH initiative page and subscribe to J-PAL newsletters. Applications were via WizeHive.

name: Fondation Mérieux Small Grants Programme
amount: Up to €5,000. The project's budget excluding the grant must be €50,000 or less.
countries: Vietnam
eligibility: Local non-profits registered for at least 3 years, in Fondation Mérieux's eligible countries. Of the 10, only Vietnam is listed. Individuals and student associations are excluded.
deadline: Two sessions a year: 1 Dec – 1 Mar and 1 May – 1 Aug. Next window opens 1 Dec 2026, deadline 1 Mar 2027.
status_note: Closed (session 2 of 2026 ended 1 Aug). Reopens 1 Dec 2026.
what: Small local projects against infectious diseases in vulnerable groups, especially mothers and children. Research-only and awareness-only projects are excluded.
mechanisms: Small grant (two sessions a year).
how: Complete the online small-grant request form on the Fondation Mérieux site when the session opens.

name: Gates Foundation AI calls and the US$1B equitable-AI commitment
amount: Varies. The recent family-planning AI RFP offered up to US$500,000 for 12 months. Amounts under the US$1B commitment are not stated.
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: The US$1B pledge will scale up 'partners that are already working' in this space. The press release describes no new open call or portal. Horizon1000 is government- and partner-led with no public application route. When Grand Challenges AI RFPs open, they usually admit organisations (not individuals) worldwide, but focus countries vary: the family-planning RFP targeted sub-Saharan Africa and preferred organisations with an existing user base. As of 28 Sep 2026 no AI RFP is listed on gcgh.grandchallenges.org.
deadline: No open AI call. None announced since the 14 Sep 2026 pledge.
status_note: Expected, with no call open now. The family-planning AI RFP closed 25 Aug 2026. The US$1B pledge is flowing to existing partners so far. New AI RFPs are plausible in the next 12 months but unconfirmed.
what: AI-for-health work in LMICs: Grand Challenges AI RFPs, co-funded evaluations (EVAH) and, from Sep 2026, a pledge of at least US$1B over two years for equitable AI. About 40% of the pledge is for health: diagnostics, decision support for frontline health workers, maternal and newborn tools, and drug and vaccine discovery.
mechanisms: US$1B commitment announced 14 Sep 2026 with the Goalkeepers Report. Past Grand Challenges AI RFPs: Catalyzing Equitable AI Use (2023, including LLM calls), AI-enabled family planning (closed 25 Aug 2026), AI for charitable giving. Horizon1000 with OpenAI (US$50M, 1,000 African primary-care clinics, starting in Rwanda). EVAH (see separate entry).
how: Subscribe to Grand Challenges alerts at gcgh.grandchallenges.org. Check the grant-opportunities page monthly. Build partnerships with existing Gates AI grantees in-country.

name: Grand Challenges India (GCI)
funder: BIRAC / Department of Biotechnology (Govt of India) with Gates Foundation (and Wellcome)
amount: Screening & Diagnosis 2026: INR 50 lakh to INR 2 crore depending on stage.
countries: India

deadline: Screening & Diagnosis call opened 12 May 2026. It was due 1 Jul 2026, extended to 15 Jul 2026. No open GCI call as of 28 Sep 2026.
status_note: Closed. No new GCI call listed on BIRAC's call-for-proposals page. Further calls are expected but no date is given.
what: India-specific Grand Challenges calls in health, nutrition, agriculture and AI. The most recent call was 'Breakthrough Solutions and Cost-Disruptive Innovations for Screening and Diagnosis' (TB, emerging pathogens, syndromic testing, enteric pathogens; point-of-care, ultra-low-cost).
mechanisms: Thematic calls, e.g. Screening & Diagnosis 2026, Catalyzing Equitable AI Use (2023), TB cachexia, climate & health.
how: Register on the BIRAC portal (birac.nic.in/cfp.php). Watch the GCI site for new calls.

name: Wellcome Leap programs
funder: Wellcome Leap (Wellcome-founded, US 501(c)(3)), with co-funders such as Bayer and Pivotal Ventures
amount: Program totals about US$50–55M. Per-project amounts vary (e.g., up to US$5M reported for Focused Antibiotics).
countries: Dominican Republic; Jamaica; Armenia; India; Thailand; Vietnam; Philippines; Uganda; Zimbabwe; Botswana
eligibility: Any legal entity in any jurisdiction: universities, research institutes, companies, non-profits, government bodies. Small agile teams are welcome; large consortia are not required. The MARFA must be signed before an award.

how: Sign up for program updates at wellcomeleap.org. When a program opens, download the program announcement and submit a 7-page abstract through the smapply portal.

name: Rockefeller Foundation Bellagio Center – Residencies and Convenings

eligibility: Residency is open to academics, artists and senior practitioners of any nationality; current holders of public office are excluded. Convenings must be sponsored by an organisation with a charitable purpose. Rockefeller does not accept unsolicited grant proposals.

mechanisms: Bellagio Residency (annual call). Bellagio Group Convenings (rolling, reviewed quarterly).
how: Sign up for Bellagio program alerts. When the call opens, submit an expression of interest at residency.rockefellerfoundation.org. For convenings, contact bellagioapplicant@rockfound.org.

funder: Gates Foundation (profiled with Science for Africa Foundation)
